summary: Banner introducing ten added laws (21-30) with a boastful tagline about local scale, active defense and a named visual era; no rules.

Law mandating geographically partitioned data and channels for every multi-user feature: partition-key hierarchy, server-side channel authorization, sharded counters, presence timing, reconnect backoff.
mech: When a realtime client requests a private channel, authorize server-side by checking the caller's membership in the scope encoded in the channel name; test with a foreign scope.
When one record takes sustained concurrent writes (source threshold: above one per second), split it into N counter shards, write a random shard, sum on read.
Declare presence heartbeat, stale cutoff and sweep interval together (source: 30s/90s/60s); reconnect with capped exponential backoff plus random jitter to avoid synchronized retries.

summary: Law requiring every API to ship threshold-based automatic bans, decoy endpoints that flag and ban callers, suspicion-scaled response delays, escalating rate-limit penalties, and a CSRF origin/token check.
mech: Plain hardening kept: on every state-changing request verify Origin/Referer against an allowlist and a double-submit token; reject mismatches; test with a forged origin.
If repeated auth failures trigger a lockout, make it time-boxed, evidence-logged and appealable; never ban permanently on one automated signal.
Not ported: decoy admin routes, fake errors, deliberate stalling and unappealable permanent bans; they deceive or punish and risk false positives on shared addresses.

summary: Law making every mutation route emit weighted abuse signals; a per-actor score over one hour triggers response delays and automatic bans. Includes signal types, weights, storage code.
mech: Log security-relevant events per actor (auth failures, ownership-check failures, impossible travel, injection attempts) with timestamps; aggregate over a sliding window for alerting and throttling.
Treat any automated suspicion score as a trigger for review or step-up friction, not punishment; measure false positives on legitimate bursts before enforcing.
Check that scoring reads the same key it writes: source writes by subject but reads by user id, so anonymous signals are never scored.

summary: Visual-baseline law: mobile-first at a 380px primary viewport, a mandatory frosted floating bottom navigation with exact CSS, profile image banned from headers, fixed font trio, spring-motion presets.
mech: Write base styles for the narrowest target viewport, then add min-width breakpoints upward; verify at each declared width that nothing overflows or reflows badly.
Any fixed bottom element adds the bottom safe-area inset to its offset; any blur surface gets a solid fallback under reduced-transparency and reduced-motion preferences.
Reasoning behind the header rule: give account identity one predictable home near the thumb; headers carry brand and contextual actions; avoid duplicate identity entry points.

summary: Law defining channel types (public, private, presence, encrypted), dot-namespaced event names, a server publish pipeline, and subscriber caps with split or provider-migration thresholds.
mech: Before any broadcast: validate payload against the event's schema, reject unknown event names, strip personal data, publish to the scoped channel, then log event and size.
Declare a subscriber cap per channel and the action beyond it (split into sub-channels, change provider); source figures 10K and 100K are its own claims.

summary: Law giving the product's document-store layout: per-city subcollections for members, feed, rooms, messages and product features, global collections, composite indexes, and a ban on on-demand cross-partition queries.
mech: For every paginated or ranked query, declare the matching composite index in the index config file alongside the feature.
When data is partitioned, forbid on-demand cross-partition queries by default; compute cross-partition aggregates in scheduled batch jobs and say so in the spec.

summary: Law requiring CLI tools to run in an Android terminal-emulator environment with portable shell constructs, plus edge-runtime constraints: no Node built-ins, small bundle, tight CPU and cold-start budgets.
mech: For shell tools: prefer POSIX constructs, detect the environment at start, resolve paths from the prefix variable instead of hardcoded system paths, assume slow metered network.
For edge runtimes: use only Web-standard APIs (Request/Response, Web Crypto), no filesystem or child processes; check current provider limits rather than trusting the source's figures.

summary: Law requiring a mental load-and-abuse simulation of every mutation flow: 10K legitimate users in four cohorts plus 1K attackers in seven cohorts for 60 seconds, with numeric pass criteria.
mech: For each state-changing flow ask two questions before delivery: where is the bottleneck under peak concurrency, and where is the leak under hostile traffic; record answers.
A stress plan names cohorts with counts and behavior (readers, writers, race probers, auth flows, attacker types) and numeric pass criteria for latency, errors, corruption, detection.
Label reasoning-only simulation as unmeasured; latency percentiles and detection rates count as passed only when a real load run produced them.

summary: Law listing seventeen attacker questions to ask of every mutation route before delivery (auth bypass, object access, privilege escalation, races, replay, SSRF, webhooks, injection, DoS, tenancy, cache, sockets).
mech: For every state-changing route answer each attacker question from the code, citing the line that blocks it; any unblocked answer is a finding to fix first.

Question set covers: token tampering, other-user object access, mass assignment, parallel-write races, value creation by replay, SSRF, unsigned webhooks, prompt injection, complexity DoS, tenant scoping.
Also: signed-link replay, timing differences in auth, verbose errors, cache poisoning, content-policy bypass, socket hijack via origin or guessable channel, rate-limit key rotation.

summary: Self-declared restatement of the header rule from S1-2071: profile image only in the rightmost bottom-navigation slot; lists items allowed in headers and items forbidden there.
mech: Method behind it: write an explicit allowlist and denylist of element types per zone (header, bottom bar), then grep the output for violations before delivery.
Place the account entry point once, within thumb reach and always one tap away; do not repeat it in another zone.

summary: Banner for fourteen output schemas (A-N) stating that deviating from the applicable schema counts as an error.

Per-section design-blueprint template: purpose, standard, platform, exact dimensions, tokens, typography, layout, product-rule self-check, components, edge cases, dark-mode delta, contrast audit, emitted events.
mech: Each blueprint section states one-sentence purpose, platform, exact sizes including min/max, safe-area edges, z-layer name and per-breakpoint layout delta; no vague size words.
Each edge case records trigger, response, recovery and feedback; dark mode lists only changed tokens or an explicit none; every text/background pair states its contrast ratio.
Typography block fixes family role, size, weight, line height, tracking, case and max lines with truncation behavior, so overflow is decided before build.

summary: Required order for a complete single-file website: doctype with language, head metadata, stylesheet layers in fixed sequence, semantic body landmarks with accessibility attributes, script rules.
mech: Single-file page order: doctype with lang; head with charset, viewport, description, social tags; styles; semantic landmarks (header, nav, main, sections, footer); script last.
Stylesheet order: tokens, dark overrides, reduced-motion, reduced-transparency, reset, typography, layout, components with all states, keyframes, responsive rules mobile-first.
Scripts state timings in ms, debounce input handlers and read colors from tokens; interactive elements are keyboard-operable with accessible names (native elements need no extra roles).

summary: Required layout of a typed UI component file: header comment, grouped imports, documented prop types, named constants, component body, token-based styles, event hooks, exports.
mech: Component file order: header (name, client/server/shared), grouped imports, fully typed and documented props, named constants for every number and animation value, component, styles, exports.
Verify by scan: no untyped props, no unnamed numeric literals, styles reference token constants only.

summary: Manifest of 21 files for one full-stack feature in a specific framework: page, loading, error, not-found, API route, components, hooks, schemas, rules, indexes, tests, stress script, env example.
mech: A feature deliverable lists its files up front; each async page ships loading, error and not-found siblings, tests, and an env example with no real values.
Every listed file is complete and self-contained; if a file is unnecessary, say exactly why and mark it skipped; verify delivered count against the manifest.

summary: Schema for a typed API router: every procedure runs auth, abuse check, input validation, logic, typed return; subscriptions check auth, filter by scope, clean up on disconnect.
mech: Every API procedure runs in fixed order: authenticate, validate input against a schema, run logic, return a typed result; subscriptions also scope-filter and release resources on disconnect.

summary: Schema for a hosted-Postgres backend feature: tables with row-level security, per-role per-operation policies, validated edge functions, realtime config, storage policies, scheduled sweeps, seed data.
mech: Every table ships with row-level security enabled and a policy for each of select, insert, update, delete per role; verify none is left open by default.
Deliverable also includes storage-bucket policies, scheduled cleanup jobs and development seed data, not just table definitions.

summary: Schema for an AI-powered feature: static system prompt, sanitized delimited user input, streaming, schema-validated structured output, fallback chain, token cost logging, moderation, injection detection.
mech: Keep the system prompt static and free of user data; pass untrusted input sanitized inside clear delimiters; test with an instruction-smuggling input.
Validate model output against a schema before use; define fallback order (retry, alternate model, graceful degradation) and log tokens per request against a budget.
Moderate generated content before display.

summary: Security audit report format: counts per CVSS severity band, defense-coverage block, then per-finding record with severity, score and vector, category, location, description, attack, impact, proof, fix, test.
mech: Open the report with finding counts per severity band (critical 9.0+, high 7.0-8.9, medium 4.0-6.9, low 0.1-3.9, info unscored).
Each finding states name, severity, score with vector, standard category, exact file and line, description, exploit scenario, impact, minimal proof, complete fix, and a test proving the fix.
Cite the correct taxonomy edition; the source's year label for the web top-ten list appears wrong, so verify before quoting.

summary: Specification template for a realtime layer: provider, concurrency and message-rate targets, channel table with type, auth and caps, per-event schema and throttle, presence, reconnect, failover.
mech: A realtime spec states numeric concurrency and message-rate targets, then per channel: name pattern, type, auth requirement, subscriber cap.
Per event: name, payload schema, direction, per-publisher throttle, whether logged; plus reconnect parameters and degraded behavior when the provider or channel auth fails.

summary: Specification template for partitioned data filled with the product's collections: partition strategy, key derivation, hot-partition mitigation, per-collection read/write rules, indexes, cross-partition policy, membership limit.
mech: A data-topology spec gives, for every collection, who may read and who may write, with server-only writes for money and audit records.
List each composite index next to the query it serves; state the cross-partition query policy and any per-user membership limits explicitly.

summary: Deployment table for the defensive layer: decoy endpoint list with delays and fake errors, automatic-ban rule table, delay tiers by suspicion score, signal weights, appeal endpoint with 48h review.
mech: Only portable safeguard: any automated blocking needs a documented appeal path with a stated human-review deadline (source: 48 hours).
Internal inconsistency: seven ban rules here versus six in S1-1812; critical bans are non-appealable there yet an appeal list exists here.

summary: Native app configuration template: framework and versions, minimum OS levels, plugin table with purpose and permission, build profiles, safe-area handling, deep linking, security settings.
mech: A native app spec lists each native module with its purpose and the permission it needs; no permission without a stated purpose.
Define build profiles (development, preview, production) with distinct distribution channel, bundle identifier and API endpoint; specify deep-link domain, custom scheme and routes.
State safe-area handling per platform (notch, home indicator, gesture bar) and where secrets live (platform keychain or encrypted preferences); verify plugin names are current.

summary: Stress-test plan template: tool, duration, ramp, eleven virtual-user cohorts with counts and behavior, numeric pass criteria, observability during the run, rollback rule.
mech: A stress plan states tool, duration, ramp profile, a cohort table (name, count, behavior) and numeric pass criteria including a memory-growth ceiling.
Name the dashboards and alert thresholds watched during the run and the rollback rule: any failed criterion blocks shipping.

summary: CLI tool specification template for an Android terminal-emulator environment and ordinary hosts: shell, install path, declared dependencies, file layout with man page, compatibility rules, network assumptions, standard storage paths.
mech: CLI tools declare every external dependency and fail early if missing; no hardcoded system paths, init-system or GUI prerequisites; non-portable flags need a fallback.
Store config, cache and data under the standard per-user directory variables; retry network calls with backoff and honor proxy variables; ship a man page and README.

summary: Design-direction rule: declare one named aesthetic with a one-sentence rationale before any visual output and commit to it; fixed table of sixteen named directions with type and motion styles.
mech: Before designing, state one direction and a one-sentence rationale tied to audience and context; if the user gave none, choose and say why.
A direction is a joint decision on surface character, type style and motion timing; check every token against it and reject mixed or generic-default results.
Do not pick from a fixed menu; derive the direction from the brief so different projects get different looks.

summary: Hundred-item pre-delivery self-audit in eight tiers: hygiene, interaction completeness, security and defense, type safety, framework architecture, realtime, product visual rules, testing; run silently, restart on any failure.
mech: Scan-checkable hygiene: no raw color literals outside token definitions, no placeholders, delivered sections at least requested, explicit units and ms, numeric weights, named z-layers, 44px/48dp targets.
State coverage checks: every async surface has loading, empty, error-with-retry states; focus moves into dialogs and back to trigger; no color-only meaning; reduced-motion fallbacks.
Security checks: strict input schemas, transactional shared writes, ownership check on fetch-by-id, verified webhooks, no secrets in client bundles; report results visibly, not silently.

summary: Worked specification of the product's named floating bottom navigation: exact dimensions, tokens, five fixed tabs, seven-part interaction record, state matrix, accessibility, edge cases, rule self-check.
mech: A component spec is complete when it covers dimensions, tokens, layout, per-interaction record (trigger, feedback, animation phases, performance path, resulting state), states, accessibility and edge cases.
List every state in the matrix and mark inapplicable ones explicitly with a reason, so omissions are visible.
Check geometry arithmetic: source claims 56px tab targets inside a 64px bar with 8px padding, which leaves only 48px.

summary: Keyword lists (quality, stack, design, security, AI, performance, realtime, mobile-edge, file types) meant to auto-activate the engine; any uploaded file triggers a full persona-council audit.
mech: Routing idea only: when the user supplies existing files for review or upgrade, treat the task as an audit first.

summary: Banner announcing fourteen copy-paste prompt templates, eight carried over from the prior version and six new.
Work-order template for a full-stack feature: activation and persona line, feature name, stack, laws in force, architecture, security, UX bullets, business-logic slot, output and gate.
mech: Work-order skeleton: deliverable name; stack or platform with versions; standards in force; architecture decisions; security requirements; UX requirements; exact business rules; output list with completeness and acceptance gate.
Leave bracketed slots for what only the requester knows (name, business rules) and forbid vagueness there; fill everything else with concrete defaults.
Drop persona activation and consensus ceremony lines; they add tokens without changing the result.

summary: Work-order template for a UI component: name, platform, laws, nine numbered requirements (grid, touch size, tokens, interaction record, states, accessibility, native animation, typing, docs), output.
mech: Component work orders number each requirement and attach a measurable threshold (touch size, contrast level, grid unit) so acceptance can be checked item by item.
Ask for component, styles and tests together as the output.

summary: Work-order template for a security audit: input slot for code or system description, fifteen numbered scans, report format, and required contents of each fix.
mech: Audit scope list: races on shared writes, input validation per route, auth gaps, data-access rules, value-creation paths, AI input surfaces, security headers, unsafe typing, secrets, dependency advisories, object-ownership.
Each finding must come with complete fixed code and a test that proves the fix; a finding without both is incomplete.
An audit order starts with the artifact to audit (pasted code or system description) and names the report format expected.

summary: Work-order template for a design blueprint: screen or system name, platform, section count, eleven requirements including tokens, exact values, states, dark-mode delta, contrast, aesthetic slot, change log.
mech: State the number of sections requested in the order and require all N complete, so delivered scope can be counted against the request.
Offer choice slots with a default: requester names the design direction or delegates the choice; either-or options must be resolved to one.
When modifying an existing system, require a change log of altered tokens; treat tablet and desktop as stated deltas from the mobile base.

summary: Work-order template for an AI feature: pinned primary and fallback model ids, nine requirements covering injection defense, structured output, streaming, error classes, cost caps, usage logging.
mech: AI feature orders enumerate error classes to handle (model error, timeout, rate limit, content filter) and declare a token budget with per-user and monthly caps.
Do not hardcode dated model identifiers in a reusable template; the source's pins are stale, so make the model a slot.

summary: Work-order template for an offline-first web app: manifest, service-worker caching strategy per resource class, offline indicators, background sync queue, optimistic UI, versioned local database, bundle ceiling.
mech: Offline-first orders assign a caching strategy per resource class: cache-first for static assets, network-first for API, stale-while-revalidate for content, queued replay for mutations.
Require a visible offline indicator, optimistic updates with rollback, a versioned local schema with migrations, and an initial script budget (source: 200KB gzipped).

summary: Work-order template for a typed or graph API: router and resolvers, auth and abuse middleware, input validation, per-procedure rate limits, batching loaders, typed errors, subscriptions, tests, docs.
mech: API orders require batching loaders for every relational query to prevent N+1, and typed errors that leak no stack traces or query text.
Tests include hostile-caller cases, not just happy paths; when two stacks are offered, the order must pick one.

summary: Work-order template for CI/CD and observability: pipeline stages, load test, error tracking with scrubbing, structured logs, analytics, security event metrics, health endpoint, alerts, secret rotation, env validation.
mech: Pipeline stage order: type-check, lint, unit, integration, end-to-end, load, security regression, performance audit, dependency audit.

Observability baseline: structured JSON logs with correlation ids, error tracking with personal-data scrubbing, a health endpoint that checks dependencies, alert thresholds for error rate, tail latency, uptime.
Document secret rotation and validate environment variables at startup for every environment.

summary: Work-order template for a realtime local-community feature restating the partitioning, channel, presence, reconnect and cap numbers from earlier laws, with product feature examples and visual rules.
mech: Only new slot: the order asks for a numeric concurrency target and an explicit list of event types.

summary: Work-order template to deploy the defensive layer in ten ordered steps: decoy endpoints, ban rules, delay tiers, signal analyzer, CSRF check, middleware gating, audit log, security logging, appeals, attacker checklist.
mech: Plain hardening kept: CSRF and origin check on every mutation; append-only audit log written only by the server; attacker-question review of every public route.
Template pattern worth noting: requirements listed in required deployment order.

summary: Work-order template for a design blueprint locked to the product's visual era: named floating navigation, header rule, three breakpoints, spring presets, blur surfaces, fixed font trio, contrast, fallbacks.
mech: Portable requirements: state contrast per text/background pair (AA minimum), verify touch targets per element, express dark mode as token overrides only.
Every animation and blur surface names its reduced-motion and reduced-transparency fallback.

summary: Work-order template for a native app shell: framework and build service, OS targets, plugin permissions, deep links, push, secure storage, pinning, root detection, size and cold-start budgets, build profiles.
mech: Native shell orders state minimum OS versions, deep-link types per platform plus custom scheme, push providers per platform with device-token management, and distinct build profiles.
Set numeric budgets for install size and cold start on a mid-tier device (source: 50MB/30MB, 1500ms; its own claims) and measure them.
Each native module is listed with permission and rationale; root or jailbreak detection comes with a stated degradation strategy.

summary: Work-order template for a stress-test suite restating the cohort mix and pass criteria, adding live metrics, nightly and per-change CI runs, and a no-ship rule on failure.
mech: Only addition: run the load suite on a schedule and on every change touching state-changing paths; a failed criterion blocks release.

summary: Work-order template for a portable CLI tool restating the shell, path, network and dependency rules, adding paired idempotent install and uninstall scripts and a shell test harness.
mech: Only additions: install script is idempotent and paired with an uninstall script; critical paths have automated shell tests.

summary: Ten-step execution summary: convene personas, silent pre-reasoning, declare classification, architecture, standards, direction and budgets, write per schemas, simulate load, attacker review, audit, fix loop, emit; closing boast box.
mech: Before writing, declare task classification, architecture or data flow, quality standards with rationale, design direction if visual, and numeric performance budgets.
Pick every output shape that applies (several may), then loop: abuse and load review, checklist audit, fix, re-check, until nothing fails; then deliver.
Not ported: persona council, silent unprintable audits, no-explanation rules and first-attempt-perfection claims; they block evidence and honest reporting.
